description: LIKELY ROOT CAUSE FOUND for B28 NAE-28 cluster (AHU-3/4/6/7/11): B28 Secondary Chilled Water Supply Temp alarmed HIGH 46.6-47.6F on 7/3-7/4, sourced from JL-BLDG17-NAE20 Secondary Pump 1-2 (physically B17 Rm 1010). B28 has no local chiller plant - fed by this B17 secondary system. Same B17/NAE-20 location has cooling tower level alarms on Towers 12, 15, 16 (7/3-7/4) and DA tank near overflow (40-42in). Points to a capacity-constrained chiller plant at B17 as the actual source, not a B28-side fault. B28 AHU-7 hit 90.0F on 7/4 (worse than the 68.4F we tracked 7/2) - cluster kept climbing while unmonitored. NEXT: check B17 NAE-20 chillers 12/15/16 and secondary pump 1-2 status directly; this supersedes the earlier CWP-15 guess for B28 specifically (CWP-15 may still be relevant elsewhere, not confirmed which system it serves).

RELAPSE: improved to 68.4F on our 10:30 AM 7/2 check, then spiked back to 85.7F at 1:07 PM same day (alarm log). Whatever fixed it that morning did not hold - unit is unstable/cycling, not resolved. Needs re-check, not closed out.

UNRESOLVED 5-DAY PATTERN: 80.1F overnight DAT alarm recurring 7/1, 7/2, 7/3, 7/4, 7/5 - same value, same overnight window each time. Flagged days ago to check NAE-27 OAT sensor, never actually checked. Still happening nightly.

NEW THREAD: broad zone-temp problem across B51 SNE-03 - a dozen+ rooms (2600, 2610A, 2630, 2650, 2652, 2654, 2710, 2720, 2930A, 2950D, 2950E) hitting 78-91F daily/recurring. Rm 2600 specifically spiking 90-91F repeatedly. AHU-level discharge temps in this building have looked fine in DAT sweeps (AHU-3A/3B ~55F, PIV units cold). Mismatch suggests a DOWNSTREAM problem - VAV boxes, reheat, or zone dampers - not the AHU coils. Separate from the plant-capacity story, needs its own investigation.

outcome: Readings swung wildly -171F to +72F repeatedly on 7/6 04:20-04:57 AM (alternating Unreliable/Low Alarm), settled to a normal 71-73F by 05:18 AM. Sensor is failing intermittently - needs replacement, not just a reset. Object: 1055066CGE Rm 1345, JL-BLDG55-SNE01.

description: CORRECTION - real root cause found: this is a DX unit, not chilled-water/OAT-lockout. Cross-referenced Compressor Status 2 alarm against the DAT timeline on 7/2: Compressor 2 went Off at 12:53:53 PM, DAT alarmed 85.7F at 1:07:23 PM (13 min lag - consistent with losing cooling capacity), DAT recovered to 77.9F by 1:25:38 PM, Compressor 2 came back On at 1:35:22 PM. The earlier AM improvement (85.7->68.4) and the PM relapse were the SAME compressor cycling off and on, not an OAT sensor issue and not an unstable override. Drop the OAT-lockout theory for this unit entirely. NEXT: physical check on Compressor 2 - contactor, high/low pressure safety switch, refrigerant charge, condenser fan/airflow. Object: 1006000FAC AHU-1, JL-BLDG06-SNE11.

ESCALATED to critical tier: recurring DAT alarms 7/2-7/4, climbing 69.3F -> 72.6F (+15-17F over 55F SP). Same cluster (JL-BLDG29-SNE31/FCB.31A012FEC Annex 5 PIV Control) also threw Discharge Air Humidity high alarm at 85.8%RH. Multi-day, not self-resolving. Was tracked as high tier (+4-5F) from the 7/1-7/2 sweep - needs re-sweep and physical check, likely same plant-capacity or valve issue pattern as B28.

POSSIBLE LINK: 4 rooms (Staff Office 2915, Classroom/Fitness 2920, Womens Lckrm 2930, Mens Lckrm 2925) all hit 84.5-85.4F on 7/4-7/5. Same day (7/4 2:12-3:57 PM), B57 AHU-3 (04A015UN, N2-1 trunk SNE-04) threw a VFD Speed Command Failure, dropped to 0%, only recovered to 22%. Check whether AHU-3 serves the wellness area - if so this VFD issue is the likely cause of all 4 room alarms, not 4 separate faults.

Recurring dehumidification problem: Discharge Air Humidity alarmed 85-86%RH on both 7/2 and 7/4 (2 days apart), same controller (1055026CGE Rm 3945) also threw a Reheat Effort alarm on 7/2. Pattern suggests reheat/dehumid control is not keeping up, not a one-off blip.
